skill.name: diffdock
skill.description: Guide Claude and compatible coding agents through DiffDock molecular docking workflows, including setup, batch preparation, pose prediction, and confidence-score analysis.
skill.summary: Run and interpret DiffDock protein-ligand docking workflows with setup checks, batch CSV validation, and result analysis.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives after reviewing the cited files. The skill contains DiffDock documentation and helper scripts that print setup guidance, validate local CSV inputs, and analyze local results; no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden command execution was found.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes many shell and Docker commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands clearly labeled as examples and require the user to approve any execution in Claude Code or similar tools.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write user-requested output files.
remediation.suggestion: Continue documenting output paths clearly so users understand when files such as CSV summaries are created.

content.value_statement: Molecular docking workflows require careful setup, validated inputs, and cautious result interpretation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through DiffDock setup, docking runs, batch screening, and confidence-score analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explain when DiffDock is appropriate for protein-ligand pose prediction.
Guide local DiffDock installation with conda or Docker examples.
Create and validate batch CSV inputs for multiple docking jobs.
Run single-complex, sequence-based, and batch docking workflows.
Analyze DiffDock confidence scores and rank predicted poses.
Suggest parameter changes for sampling density, inference steps, and ligand flexibility.
limitations: Does not predict binding affinity, dissociation constants, or free energy directly.
Requires a working DiffDock installation and suitable compute resources for execution.
Needs scientific validation before using predictions for drug discovery decisions.
May underperform for covalent docking, protein-protein docking, large peptides, or unusual ligands.

use_cases.title: Dock a Lead Compound
use_cases.description: Prepare a protein and ligand, run DiffDock, and inspect the top predicted binding poses.

use_cases.title: Screen a Ligand Library
use_cases.description: Build a batch CSV, validate inputs, run virtual screening, and rank predicted poses by confidence.

use_cases.title: Tune Docking Parameters
use_cases.description: Adjust samples, inference steps, and temperature settings for difficult ligands or flexible proteins.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Docking Inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup before a first run
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a protein PDB file and a ligand SMILES string. Help me confirm whether DiffDock is suitable and prepare the first command.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Batch Docking Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create and validate a DiffDock batch CSV for these protein-ligand pairs, then explain the command I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Docking Results
prompt_templates.scenario: After DiffDock has generated SDF files and scores
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my DiffDock result directory, summarize confidence scores, and explain which poses need visual inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Difficult Docking Campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced parameter tuning and downstream validation
prompt_templates.prompt: My DiffDock predictions have low confidence for a flexible ligand library. Recommend parameter changes, ensemble options, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Dock aspirin to a prepared protein structure.
output_examples.output: The skill would confirm the input types, suggest a single-complex DiffDock command, explain expected output files, and remind you that confidence is not affinity.

output: Create a batch CSV with required columns.
Validate protein paths and ligand descriptions.
Run batch inference with an appropriate batch size.
Analyze and rank poses by confidence.

output_examples.input: All poses have low confidence scores.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend checking protein preparation, increasing sample counts, considering ensemble docking, and using visual inspection plus rescoring.

best_practices: Validate protein structures, ligand formats, and batch CSV files before long runs.
Use GPU resources when possible because CPU docking can be very slow.
Combine DiffDock confidence with visualization, rescoring, and experimental validation.
anti_patterns: Treating confidence scores as binding affinity or final hit ranking.
Running large virtual screens before testing one small example successfully.
Using DiffDock for covalent docking, protein-protein docking, or unsupported large biomolecules.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan, run, and interpret DiffDock molecular docking workflows for protein-ligand pose prediction.

faq.question: Does DiffDock predict binding affinity?
faq.answer: No. DiffDock predicts binding poses and confidence scores. Use rescoring or experimental assays for affinity decisions.

faq.question: Can I use a protein sequence instead of a PDB file?
faq.answer: Yes. DiffDock can use ESMFold for protein sequence folding, but this adds computation time and uncertainty.

faq.question: Can this skill run virtual screening?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for batch CSV preparation, batch inference, and ranking predicted poses.

faq.question: Do I need a GPU?
faq.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended. CPU execution can take much longer and is not practical for large batches.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
